Love to see progress here.  I'm in full support of getting this done.
Because this is security code, can we can a simple unit test or two for this?  Doesn't have to be extensive.
Got it! I have added the unit tests for `getCommonNameFromCert` and `getUPNFromCert` functions. Let me know if you have any feedback on the test
Thank you.
nit, declare your variables where they're used.  Static analyzers complain if variables aren't initialized, so we tend to declare in the scope they're used.
Acknowledged
Can this be split on a couple of lines with some intermediates for the params?  as-written it's a little rough to read.
Acknowledged

This looks like it's going to return the UPN as-is?  getUsernameFromCert is expecting to return a username string local to this bmc.  I think some level of UPN parsing is required to verify:

A. This bmc matches the hostname the UPN points to.
B. Extract the username from the UPN string.

Hi Ed, is there a spec dictating how an UPN should look like? AFAICT the UPN field can be free-form. The redfish spec mentions:

> This value shall indicate the service matches the User Principal Name (UPN) field in the provided certificate to the UserName property in a ManagerAccount resource or the appropriate field from an external account provider.

In our usage, we've added the UPN field to match a local BMC username as an exact match (as we didn't want to introduce parsing logic that's specific to our org here)

UPNs look like email addresses, so it would be something like

marco@this_bmc.facebook.com

Or if you want to authorize a given cert against all BMCs (which seems like a bad idea from a security perspective, but you do you)

marco@facebook.com

Presumably we need to strip of the portion that looks like an email.
Hi Ed, thanks for your comments! We have implemented the steps that you mentioned (matching the hostname-UPN and extract the username). Let us know if you have any concerns on this, thanks!

> steps that you mentioned

This kind of statement worries me.  This shouldn't be an "Ed told you to do it this way" It should be in some kind of spec.  I highly recommend reaching out to DMTF (Where I'm also present in the forums and on github) and see how this is intended to be implemented at a Redfish level and if they used any other specs for that.  I would ideally like to see that show up in your commit message, again, so we're not playing the "Ed told us to do it this way" game.  If we're making decisions beyond what the spec allows, that's when I can help you decide how OpenBMC should implement things where the spec gives backends freedom, but I don't believe the parsing of UPN is one of those things.

Hi Ed, thanks for your feedbacks. I tried to search for official spec of the UPN format/parsing. The best sources that I can find are the official Microsoft website

It is stated that the UPN follows the RFC 822[1][2], which explain about the email format. The format is: someone@example.com (in the form of an email address) [3]. By convention, this should map to the user email name [1][2]. The UPN consists of 3 parts[4]:

---
| **Part**                                         | **Example**           |
|--------------------------------------------------|-----------------------|
| User account name. Also known as the logon name. | UserName              |
| Separator. A character literal, the at sign (@). | @                     |
| UPN suffix. Also known as the domain name.       | Example.Microsoft.com |
---

Domain name in the UPN identifies the domain in which the user account is located [3].

Based on the explanation from the specs, I believe our implementation is aligned with the specifications. However, If you feel that this specification may not be entirely sufficient, please let us know. We would be more than happy to reach out to DMTF, to gather more information and ensure we are implementing it correctly

---
[1] UPN Attributes: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/adschema/a-userprincipalname
[2] UPN Properties: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/ad/naming-properties#userprincipalname
[3] UPN Glossary: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-wcce/719b890d-62e6-4322-b9b1-1f34d11535b4#gt_9d606f55-b798-4def-bf96-97b878bb92c6
[4] UPN Format: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/secauthn/user-name-formats#user-principal-name
All of this is great information, and should be in some combination of your code comments and/or commit message.

I am not entirely sure whether this is the best approach to bypass the lint error `cppcoreguidelines-pro-type-union-access`

- This lint rule prevent us to access union value and strongly suggest to use the std::variant
  - However, in this case, the union definition is defined in the openssl library and we need to access the union if we want to access the value
  - We also add validation using the `nid` and `type`
- I have tried to check any presedence on this lint rule, but I cannot find any

Please let me know if we have better approach on this
Bypassing it where neccesary is fine.  In new code, std::reinterpret_cast<char*> can generally be replaced by std::bit_cast, which is safer and doesn't throw the warning.
Thanks for the feedback! will try to change it to use `bit_cast`

Hi Ed, I put the details of the test steps on the link here https://justpaste.it/adq6g . I forgot to mention to setup the UPN certificate as the first step

I also tried to use the `generate_auth_certificate.py` script, but unfortunately it is not working properly on my end. It failed on `test_mtls_auth` func. Let me know if my test plan is already sufficient. In the meantime, I will try to investigate why the error happens and get back to this later  

---
- Check UPN field on X509 certificate
```
$ sudo openssl x509 -in $THRIFT_TLS_CL_CERT_PATH -text | grep "UPN"
                othername: UPN::obmc.user_malikrafsan
```
- Make sure the UPN name exist inside the bmcweb accounts
```
$ curl --cert $THRIFT_TLS_CL_CERT_PATH --key $THRIFT_TLS_CL_KEY_PATH https://$HOSTNAME/redfish/v1/AccountService/Accounts | grep "obmc.user_malikrafsan"
      "@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/AccountService/Accounts/obmc.user_malikrafsan"
```
